title: Super Tic-Tac-Toe: Nine Boards, One Match
author: Jason Lamb
excerpt: A mobile-friendly strategy game with nine linked boards, classic modes, computer play, undo and redo, and optional private score history.

cover.alt: Glowing nine-board tic-tac-toe game with highlighted playable boards and X and O pieces

content_html:
Super Tic-Tac-Toe expands the familiar three-by-three grid into nine connected mini-boards. The cell chosen in one board sends the next player to the corresponding board. If that destination is complete, the next player can choose any available board. Winning three mini-boards in a row wins the match.

The same app also offers classic three-by-three, four-by-four, and five-by-five games. Visitors can play against another person on the same device or choose a computer opponent and difficulty level. Highlights show the last move, playable area, and winning line. Undo and redo make it easy to examine a move without starting over.

Anonymous visitors can play immediately. The browser keeps their results locally. Signed-in members with access to the project can save aggregate results and recent games in private server storage, but gameplay moves and board contents are not uploaded.

It is a compact game with a useful mix of accessibility and state management: the larger board changes where a move is allowed, while optional score saving stays separate from ordinary public play.
